about.title: Pleasant Hill Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a family in Pleasant Hill loses someone to a preventable crash, the grief is compounded by confusion about what comes next. Contra Costa County recorded 144 injury collisions and two traffic deaths in the most recent final crash year, numbers that translate into real families facing sudden, life-altering loss. Corridors like I-680, Monument Boulevard, and Contra Costa Boulevard see steady traffic, and collisions on these roads sometimes turn fatal. California law allows certain surviving family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, to pursue a wrongful death claim to recover funeral costs, lost financial support, and the value of the guidance and companionship that was lost. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect grieving families with an independent, contingency-based attorney who can explain options clearly and handle the legal work while you focus on your family.

items.title: Standing Rules Are Specific
items.desc: California limits who can file a wrongful death claim, generally starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children before other dependents or heirs. An attorney can clarify who in your family qualifies before any deadline passes.

items.title: A Strict Two-Year Window
items.desc: Wrongful death claims in California generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity was involved. Connecting with an attorney early protects your family's ability to pursue a claim.

items.title: No Fee Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning your family pays nothing upfront and no fee unless money is recovered on your behalf.

items.question: Who in my family can actually file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children to bring the claim. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing. An attorney can review your specific family situation to confirm who qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to file after losing someone in a Pleasant Hill crash?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. That deadline is shorter if a government agency, like a public road authority, may be involved. Because Pleasant Hill's busiest corridors include roads maintained by different agencies, it's worth confirming the timeline quickly.

items.question: What costs can a wrongful death claim actually cover?
items.answer: Recoverable losses typically include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the deceased would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. This is separate from any criminal case tied to the crash. An independent attorney can walk your family through what applies to your circumstances.
